we have created an open dataset of photographs and CGs that is the largest and most heterogeneous dataset of this type to date.

we have created a large and heterogeneous database of CG and PG images, we have implemented 13 methods from the state of the art, and we have developed a framework to automatically combine them, obtaining a classification accuracy of 97% for CG vs. PG

we have implemented a total of thirteen methods, and that we have achieved up to 97% accuracy in classifying computer generated images versus real photographs when combining the best methods using a fusion scheme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel and robust method to distinguish between CGs and PGs.

the development of a complete study of the state of the art in the field, the creation of a large and heterogeneous database for training and testing, the implementation of several representative methods of the scientific literature and, the development of automatic methods for combining the best of them.

the following: (1) a complete review of the literature; (2) the creation of an image dataset for training and validation; (3) the implementation of representative methods from the literature; (4) the creation of a set of fusion methods; (5) a comparative study of all methods; and (6) the evaluation of fusion schemes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a combination of the best approaches can achieve a very good performance.
, in order to obtain the best results, the most suitable combination of features and classifier is the one which takes advantage of the best features of the individual classifiers.
the proposed methods and fusion schemes are capable of achieving a very high accuracy in the classification of CGs and PGs, which is the main goal of this work.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a large dataset, we implemented and tested several CG vs. PG methods, and we devised automatic ways for combining methods.
the combination of several approaches is the best way of solving the problem of differentiating CG from PG.
the proposed fusion schemes are able to improve the accuracy of the individual classifiers by up to 97%.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a set of classifiers and features can improve the classification accuracy of computer generated images versus photographs.
the use of a combination of methods, each one with a different approach, is a promising way to improve the classification accuracy.
the use of a set of classifiers, each one focusing on a different image feature, can achieve a better performance than any individual method.
